issues.legal_issue: Opinion evidence did not establish the claimed spiritual-disciple relationship when it failed the statutory test and the sole witness claiming direct knowledge was not trustworthy.
material_facts: In a suit to recover institutional property on the basis of a claimed succession to the office of Mahant, several witnesses gave evidence about the claimant's relationship as a Chela, but their testimony did not satisfy the test for opinion evidence.
One witness claimed to have been present when the claimant was initiated as a Chela, but the Court found that witness neither trustworthy nor sufficient.
issues.conclusion: The claimed relationship as a Chela was not proved.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 50 of the Evidence Act, opinion evidence about a relationship must satisfy the statutory test. The Court relied on Dolgobinda Paricha v. Nimai Charan Misra in assessing that evidence.

rule.if: institutional_property_succession_suit and claimed_disciple_relationship and opinion_testimony_fails_statutory_test and sole_direct_witness_untrustworthy

predicates.institutional_property_succession_suit: A claimant brought a suit to recover institutional property by claiming succession to an office connected with the institution.
predicates.claimed_disciple_relationship: The claimant asserted that the prior office-holder had accepted the claimant as a spiritual disciple.
predicates.opinion_testimony_fails_statutory_test: Witnesses gave opinions about the relationship, but their testimony did not meet the legal test for such opinion evidence.
predicates.sole_direct_witness_untrustworthy: The only witness who claimed personal presence at the formation of the relationship was found not trustworthy.

issues.definition: When a claimant relies on a spiritual-disciple relationship in an institutional property succession suit, failure of the opinion evidence to meet the statutory test and lack of a trustworthy direct witness means the relationship is not proved.

issues.legal_issue: A denial of pleaded facts asserting a custom puts the claimant to proof when the answer denies those allegations without separately addressing each fact.
material_facts: The claimant pleaded a custom governing succession to the institution in two paragraphs of the original plaint.
The defendant denied the allegations in those paragraphs but did not separately address each pleaded fact.
issues.conclusion: The denial was sufficient to require the claimant to prove the alleged custom.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished Badat and Co. v. East India Trading Co. and Surendra Nath Birba v. Stephen Court Ltd.; on the pleadings in this case, the denial put the claimant to proof.

predicates.civil_suit_based_on_customary_succession: A claimant brought a civil suit relying on a custom to establish succession to an institutional office or property.
predicates.custom_alleged_in_pleading: The claimant set out the asserted custom in the original pleading.
predicates.custom_denied_without_separate_specific_: The opposing party denied the allegations containing the custom but did not separately respond to each fact pleaded.

issues.definition: In a civil suit based on customary succession, pleading a custom followed by a denial that does not separately address each fact still requires the claimant to prove the custom.

issues.legal_issue: A customary rule of succession was not proved by an isolated instance in a record that also described a different succession and was unsupported by other evidence.
material_facts: No oral evidence was presented to prove the alleged custom.
A revenue mutation order recorded the succession of one office-holder by another and also an earlier succession that did not follow the same pattern.

The order did not show that the earlier succession or the later succession to the office-holder whose properties were disputed occurred under the alleged custom, and no other oral or documentary evidence was produced.
issues.conclusion: The alleged custom was not proved.
issues.legal_principle: A custom relied on to establish succession must be supported by cogent and reliable evidence; the recorded instances in this case did not establish a consistent custom. The Court agreed with the High Court's assessment of the evidence.

rule.if: customary_succession_claim and no_oral_custom_evidence and mutation_record_contains_inconsistent_succession_instances and no_other_custom_evidence

predicates.customary_succession_claim: A claimant relied on an asserted custom to establish succession to an institutional office.
predicates.no_oral_custom_evidence: The claimant presented no oral testimony to establish the asserted custom.
predicates.mutation_record_contains_inconsistent_su: A revenue record described succession instances that did not all follow the same pattern.
predicates.no_other_custom_evidence: The claimant produced no other evidence establishing the asserted custom.

issues.definition: When a customary succession claim rests on no oral evidence, a record of differing succession instances, and no other supporting evidence, the custom is not proved.

issues.legal_issue: An asserted installation as the successor to an institutional office was not established by an unreliable record and oral evidence that the courts rejected.
material_facts: The claimant asserted that he had been installed as Mahant and relied on an entry in a Bahi as evidence of the installation.
The High Court did not accept the Bahi entry, and the Supreme Court agreed with that assessment.
The High Court also rejected the oral evidence that the claimant had been installed by the religious community or with the consent of local residents, and the Supreme Court agreed.
issues.conclusion: The claimant did not prove that he had been installed as Mahant.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the documentary and oral evidence supporting the alleged installation and found no reliable basis to disturb the High Court's rejection of it.

rule.if: institutional_office_succession_suit and installation_claimed and installation_record_unreliable and supporting_oral_testimony_rejected

predicates.institutional_office_succession_suit: A claimant sued to establish succession to an office managing an institution and its property.
predicates.installation_claimed: The claimant asserted that a community or other relevant group had installed the claimant in the office.
predicates.installation_record_unreliable: The documentary entry relied on to show installation was not accepted as reliable evidence.
predicates.supporting_oral_testimony_rejected: The courts rejected the oral testimony offered to support the claimed installation.

issues.definition: In a suit claiming succession to an institutional office, an unreliable installation record and rejected supporting testimony mean the claimed installation is not proved.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant seeking possession must establish the basis of the claimant's own right even if the opposing party has not established title to the office or property.
material_facts: The claimant sued for possession of the institution and its properties on the basis of his asserted status as the duly installed Mahant.
The claimant did not establish the claimed Chela relationship, the custom governing succession, or his installation as Mahant, and he never obtained possession of the office or properties.
The opposing party's entitlement was disputed, but the claimant's failure to establish the grounds of his own claim remained decisive.
issues.conclusion: No decree for possession could be made for the claimant, even assuming the opposing party had not established a right or title to the office or properties.
issues.legal_principle: A claimant seeking possession on a particular asserted right must prove the facts forming the basis of that right; failure by the opposing party to establish title does not itself prove the claimant's case.

rule.if: suit_for_possession_of_institutional_property and claimant_relies_on_succession_right and claimant_fails_to_prove_basis_of_right and opposing_title_not_established

predicates.suit_for_possession_of_institutional_pro: A claimant brought a suit seeking possession of property belonging to an institution.
predicates.claimant_relies_on_succession_right: The claimant based the request for possession on an asserted succession to the institution's managing office.
predicates.claimant_fails_to_prove_basis_of_right: The claimant did not prove the facts on which the asserted succession right depended.
predicates.opposing_title_not_established: The opposing party's right or title to the office or property was not established.

issues.definition: In a suit for institutional property based on succession, failure to prove the claimant's asserted right prevents a possession decree even when the opposing party's title is not established.
